title: Can I read to you Three Stories in One? | Dylan Puri | TEDxNewtons Grove Youth
description: In my opinion, the most significant shift of the next decade won't be artificial intelligence itself, but the disappearance of friction: the speed bumps that once gave us time to think, to pause, to choose who we want to be, have become “less bumpy.” We live in a world of dominoes falling faster than ever, and hopefully today I can help you learn how to be the one who steers those dominoes rather than be knocked down by someone else’s chain reaction. My name is Dylan Puri, and I am a Grade 12 student at Newton's Grove School. I want to shift away from the notion that the future is something that simply "happens to us" and realize that even as the dominoes fall faster around us, we can still set our future in motion—one decision at a time. As I've observed the world around us, I've also noticed a quiet trade-off nobody talks about: we're optimizing everything while accidentally optimizing the human parts that make life worth living. An AI revolution might be inevitable, but realize that there are two paths that can be forged: those who get swept away and those who learn to steer. title: British couple held for months by Taliban released from prison | BBC News
description: A British couple who were detained for nearly eight months by the Taliban in Afghanistan have been released, an official with knowledge of the case has said. Peter Reynolds, 80, and his wife Barbie, 76, who have lived in the country for nearly two decades, were held after being stopped while travelling home on 1 February. The couple were freed through Qatari mediation, after they were transferred from Kabul's central prison to a larger prison during the final phase of negotiations, the official said. A Qatari official said the couple will fly to Qatar for medical checks before travelling on to the UK, despite having a long-term home in Afghanistan's Bamiyan province. It follows months of public lobbying by their family for their release. Six days ago, an American woman who was detained with them and subsequently released told the BBC they were "literally dying" in prison and that "time is running out". title: Trump warns Iran “massive armada” on way and time running out for nuclear deal | BBC News
description: Donald Trump has warned Iran that "time is running out" to negotiate a deal on its nuclear programme following the build-up of US military forces in the Gulf. The US president said a "massive Armada" was "moving quickly, with great power, enthusiasm, and purpose" towards Iran, referring to a large US naval fleet. In response, Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said the country's armed forces were ready "with their fingers on the trigger" to "immediately and powerfully respond" to any aggression by land or sea. Iran insists its nuclear programme is entirely peaceful and has repeatedly denied accusations by the US and its allies that it is seeking to develop nuclear weapons. Trump's latest warning follows his promise that Washington would intervene to help those involved in the brutal and unprecedented crackdown on protests in the country earlier this month. The US-based Human Rights Activists News Agency (HRANA) says it has confirmed the killing of more than 6,301 people, including 5,925 protesters, since the unrest began at the end of December. HRANA says it is also investigating another 17,000 reported deaths received despite an internet shutdown after nearly three weeks. Another group, the Norway-based Iran Human Rights (IHR), has warned that the final toll could exceed 25,000. Reeta Chakrabarti presents BBC News at Ten reporting by Caroline Hawley and Sarah Smith. title: From Dotcom to AI: Still Repeating Anxiety pattern | Prashant Jain | TEDxTula International School
description: We taught machines to recognise patterns. Now our own patterns are overwhelming us. From Dotcom to AI, we perfected external intelligence. But internally, we’re repeating the same anxiety loops. This talk challenges a hidden assumption: Maybe the crisis of our time isn’t artificial intelligence. It’s artificial identity. By going back to first principles — biology, consciousness, and collective intelligence — this talk offers a new lens on anxiety, acceleration, and the search for meaning. Not fear. Not rejection of technology. But integration. The question isn’t “What is AI becoming?” The question is: “Who are we becoming?” Prashant Jain is a technology entrepreneur, wellness builder, author, and speaker whose journey through disruption began in 1996, at the dawn of India’s first internet wave. He was part of the founding journey of Indiadomain.com, one of India’s earliest dotcom ventures, and worked on early e-commerce platforms such as HyderabadBazaar.com and BangaloreBazaar.com—long before digital commerce became a household habit. Trained as an engineer, he earned his Master’s degree from Wright State University, USA, and went on to build large-scale cloud platforms and digital infrastructure, including work on one of India’s largest data centers in Navi Mumbai. When the dotcom bubble burst, its impact went far beyond failed startups. Careers collapsed, identities fractured, and anxiety quietly followed. That lived experience—of rapid rise and sudden fall—became a lasting lens through which he now views progress. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at URL

title: Stubborn Tree Stumps? How to Remove Them Using Only Hand Tools
description: In my garden, I tackle stubborn tree stumps using only hand tools and no machines involved. title: UK Prime Minister facing calls to resign over ambassador’s Epstein links | BBC News
description: The British Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer is under intense political pressure, with calls for him to resign, over his decision to appoint Lord Mandelson as the UK’s ambassador to the United States, despite his links to the convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. The leader of Sir Keir’s Labour Party in Scotland, Anas Sarwar, has become the Prime Minister's most senior colleague to say he must step down for the sake of his party and the country. Sir Keir nominated Lord Mandelson for the UK’s top diplomatic post in December 2024, despite knowing he had continued his relationship with Epstein after his conviction and jail sentence. Sir Keir was forced to dismiss Lord Mandelson nine months later, when email exchanges between the two men were released. The scandal developed into a crisis threatening Sir Keir’s leadership with the recent release of documents by the US Justice Department, which appear to show that Peter Mandelson leaked market-sensitive information to Epstein when he was a government minister. Sir Keir’s chief of staff Morgan McSweeney has resigned, taking responsibility for advising the Prime Minister to appoint Lord Mandelson as ambassador. Sir Keir’s head of communications has also left his job. It is about understanding that in the process of building something meaningful, you are also being built.
